name: Crowded Crypt
oracle_text:
{T}: Add {B}.
Whenever a creature you control dies, put a corpse counter on this artifact.
{4}{B}{B}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token with decayed for each corpse counter on this artifact. (A creature with decayed can't block. When it attacks, sacrifice it at end of combat.)
blocked_sentences: {4}{B}{B}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token with decayed for each corpse counter on this artifact.

needs.what: A value that reads how many counters of a kind were on an object sacrificed as an activation cost, as last-known information (608.2h) -- e.g. the `sacrifice` cost's `as` snapshot recording the object's counters, and a value such as `{"counters_on": {"counter": "corpse", "objects": {"binding": "sacrificed"}}}` (or a `counters_had` that reads that binding) answering from it. Used as the `amount` of `create_token` with token `zombie_2_2_b_decayed`.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `counters_on` reads the live object, and the self-sacrifice cost is paid before the ability resolves, so the artifact is a graveyard card whose counters `reset_permanent_state` has already emptied -- it always reads 0. The cost's `as` binding is a `zones.snapshot`, which records power/toughness/types/colors but no counters. `counters_had` reads only the dies-trigger's `had_counters` binding, which an activated ability never gets. The `snapshot` op runs at resolution, after the source has left. The token itself exists (`zombie_2_2_b_decayed`), and the corpse-counter trigger is expressible (`creature_dies` + `add_counters`).
